title: How do we construct a rectangle seven centimetres by four?
description: A rectangle with one side seven centimetres and the next side four centimetres is constructed from a base and two perpendiculars. Keeko's doubt is that only the lengths matter, so the angles can be left out.
teaching_notes: One idea: a rectangle is built from one side, a perpendicular at each end, and the second length marked on each perpendicular. Watch for students who mark the second length on a slanting line instead of a perpendicular.

source: Construct a rectangle ABCD with AB = 7 cm and BC = 4 cm.
video_script.why: A learner constructs a rectangle from two given side lengths using perpendiculars at both ends of the base.
video_script.substitution: the book's own rectangle with one side seven centimetres and the next side four centimetres
video_script.anchor: a rectangle with one side seven centimetres and the next side four centimetres, built step by step on the board
video_script.wrong_answer: only the lengths matter, so the angles can be left out
video_script.wrong_move: marks the four centimetre length on a slanting line, so the corner is not a right angle and the top side no longer matches the base
video_script.payoff_line: The finished figure is the rectangle we wanted.

final_answer.value: Rectangle ABCD with AB = CD = 7 cm and BC = AD = 4 cm, all angles 90°

maths_rules: perpendicular at A, with AD = 4 cm; perpendicular at B, with BC = 4 cm
angle A = angle B = angle C = angle D = 90°, AB = CD = 7 cm, BC = AD = 4 cm
video_script.design: One rectangle is built in a fixed order: base, two perpendiculars with marked heights, then the top joined and checked.

beats.on_screen: title card, then a blank board with the words rectangle, seven centimetres and four centimetres

marks.ask: the two side lengths appear on the board

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a construction from your book.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>We must draw a rectangle with one side seven centimetres and the next side four centimetres.
What must we draw at each end of the seven centimetre side?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a rectangle with four right-angle marks and equal opposite sides

marks.props: the right-angle marks appear at the four corners
marks.plan: the base is drawn first and two upright lines rise from its ends

narration: <bookmark mark='props'/>A rectangle has four right angles and equal opposite sides.
<bookmark mark='plan'/>A perpendicular gives a right angle at the end of a side.
We draw the long side first, then build up from its two ends.

beats.on_screen: Given: rectangle ABCD, AB = 7 cm, BC = 4 cm
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a rectangle eigh bee cee dee with eigh bee seven centimetres and bee cee four centimetres.

marks.find: the task is written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to construct this rectangle.

marks.ab: the base AB is drawn and labelled 7 cm

narration: <bookmark mark='ab'/>Step one, draw eigh bee equal to seven centimetres.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: draw a perpendicular at A; mark D with AD = 4 cm

marks.perp: the perpendicular rises from A with its right-angle mark
marks.markd: D is marked 4 cm up the line

narration: <bookmark mark='perp'/>Step two, draw a perpendicular at eigh.
<bookmark mark='markd'/>Mark dee on it so that eigh dee is four centimetres.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: draw a perpendicular at B; mark C with BC = 4 cm

marks.perp: the perpendicular rises from B with its right-angle mark
marks.markc: C is marked 4 cm up the line

narration: <bookmark mark='perp'/>Step three, draw a perpendicular at bee.
<bookmark mark='markc'/>Mark cee on it so that bee cee is four centimetres.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: join D and C; DC = 7 cm = AB

marks.join: the top side DC is drawn
marks.same: matching ticks appear on DC and AB

narration: <bookmark mark='join'/>Step four, join dee and cee.
<bookmark mark='same'/>Dee cee measures seven centimetres, the same as eigh bee.

beats.on_screen: Answer: rectangle ABCD, AB = CD = 7 cm, BC = AD = 4 cm, all angles 90°

marks.res: the rectangle glows with its sides labelled

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The finished figure is the rectangle we wanted.
<bookmark mark='res'/>Eigh bee and dee cee are seven centimetres. Eigh dee and bee cee are four centimetres, and all angles are ninety degrees.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the finished rectangle
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: the line at A drawn leaning with eigh dee still four centimetres; the corner is marked as not ninety degrees and the picture is struck out

marks.doubt: the leaning line and the shifted top side appear
marks.fix: the corner angle lights up as not ninety degrees and the picture is struck out
marks.keep: the perpendicular is redrawn and the rectangle returns

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks only the lengths matter, so the angles can be left out.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Mark four centimetres on a leaning line, and the corner is not ninety degrees.
<bookmark mark='keep'/>The top side no longer matches the base, so the perpendicular is what keeps the figure a rectangle.
